Attainment and Attendance in Hastings

What the national model behind How to Pull the Right Lever says about the district’s secondary schools, within East Sussex and alongside Brighton and Hove. Draft for discussion.

Author
Affiliation

Adam Dennett

Bartlett Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis, University College London

Published

October 31, 2026

WarningDraft for discussion

One of the district documents for Sussex. It sits beneath the East Sussex document, and the district summary compares all of the districts. Every figure comes from published Department for Education data and the national models of How to Pull the Right Lever. Nothing uses pupil-level records. The commentary is written to a common pattern from the figures; read it as a starting point for discussion.

Summary

Hastings’s results are among the weakest of England’s districts, on an intake more disadvantaged than England’s. Its 3 state secondary schools are in Hastings and St Leonards-on-Sea.

  • Overall results: 37.8 in Attainment 8 in 2024/25, 263rd of 265 districts in England.
  • Disadvantage: 35.1% of pupils are disadvantaged, against 28.3% nationally.
  • Disadvantaged pupils average 29.5, below the national 37.8 (262nd of 265).
  • The gap between disadvantaged pupils and the rest is 13.0 points, the 119th widest of 265.

The other findings:

  • For all pupils, Hastings is 11.4 points below England. The largest pieces in the national model are absence (-3.9) and Ofsted ratings (-1.9). The district’s schools take 4.5 points beyond what the model expects.
  • For disadvantaged pupils it is 10.6 points below England. The largest pieces are absence (-4.5) and Ofsted ratings (-1.8), and the schools take 3.7 points beyond what the model expects.
  • A district effect on the published model disappears once each school’s own record is counted. On the published model Hastings differs from the rest of East Sussex for all pupils (-4.4%), non-disadvantaged pupils (-3.9%) and absence (+9.9%), but that difference belongs to particular schools, not to the place.
  • None of the 3 schools is above expectation over 2021/22 to 2024/25. The strongest is Ark Alexandra Academy (-1.9); the weakest The St Leonards Academy (-5.3).
  • Absence was 7.0% in autumn and spring 2025/26 (10.0% a year earlier), against 8.0% for England and 8.9% for East Sussex. Over 2021/22 to 2024/25 its schools ran 2.8 points above what their intakes predict, and The Hastings Academy and The St Leonards Academy more than a point above.
  • Reduced timetables run at 0.4 times the national rate, and suspensions at 3.7 times (77.8 per 100 pupils, against 21.2).
  • Disadvantaged groups are small, 50 to 101 pupils a year per school. Every school-level figure for them moves from year to year and should be read over several years.

1 About this analysis

Hastings is a district of East Sussex, not a local authority, and that shapes what can be said:

  • The national models place schools in local authorities. The “local authority effect” in this document is East Sussex’s, shared with every school in the county.
  • What is particular to Hastings shows up in its schools’ own residuals, and in the district test of Section 6.
  • Absence and exclusions are summed over the district’s 3 schools, followed through any change of URN.
  • Ranks. With 3 schools, Hastings is placed among the 264 districts in England with five or more schools. A district this small moves a long way with one school’s results.

The methods are described in full in the East Sussex document.

For all pupils, Hastings is 11.4 points below England. The pieces of at least a quarter of a point:

  • absence (-3.91);
  • Ofsted ratings (-1.95);
  • prior attainment (-1.69);
  • the level of disadvantage (-1.12);
  • being in the South East (-0.46);
  • East Sussex’s county-wide effect (+0.46);
  • and the district’s schools themselves (-4.47), beyond what the model expects.

For disadvantaged pupils, Hastings is 10.6 points below England. The pieces of at least a quarter of a point:

  • absence (-4.48);
  • Ofsted ratings (-1.76);
  • being in the South East (-1.32);
  • prior attainment (-1.12);
  • English as an additional language (-0.36);
  • the level of disadvantage (+0.36);
  • admissions (-0.30);
  • East Sussex’s county-wide effect (+0.29);
  • and the district’s schools themselves (-3.70), beyond what the model expects.

6 Is there a Hastings effect?

The district test of the East Sussex document adds a district level to the national model, with and without each school’s own record.

On the published model, Hastings differs from the rest of East Sussex for all pupils (-4.4%), non-disadvantaged pupils (-3.9%) and absence (+9.9%). With each school’s own record in the model, none of that remains: the difference belongs to particular schools, not to the district as a place.

7 Absence

  • 7.0% absence in autumn and spring 2025/26, against 8.0% for England and 8.9% for East Sussex. A year earlier it was 10.0%.
  • Persistent absence is 22.2%, against 21.6% for England.
  • Against its intake, the district’s schools run 2.77 points above what their pupils’ profiles predict, on average over 2021/22 to 2024/25.
  • The Hastings Academy and The St Leonards Academy each run more than a point above their predicted absence.

Reduced timetables account for 0.11% of sessions, against 0.29% in England, 0.4 times the national rate. The St Leonards Academy’s rate is the highest in the district.

All 3 schools are above the national average absence in 2024/25. Bringing them to it would add up to 1.8 points for all pupils, as an indication of scale.

Suspensions were 77.8 per 100 pupils in 2024/25, against 21.2 for England and 28.0 for East Sussex.

9 Questions for discussion

  1. Disadvantaged pupils. They average 29.5 in Hastings against 37.8 in England, and the district’s schools take 3.7 points for them beyond what the model expects. No school here is above expectation for them over the period; the question is what schools elsewhere with similar intakes do differently.
  2. Attendance is a lever here. Absence costs the district 3.9 points against England for all pupils, and The Hastings Academy and The St Leonards Academy run more than a point above what their intakes predict.
  3. Schools, not the place. The district’s apparent effect belongs to particular schools; the question is what is happening in them.
  4. Practice. In Hastings, suspensions run at 3.7 times the national rate. These are choices made within schools, and neighbouring districts make them differently.
  5. The county. East Sussex’s own effect for disadvantaged pupils is +0.9% (60th of 151), not distinguishable from zero. The county questions in the East Sussex document apply here as well.

Notes on method

Methods and sources are those of the East Sussex document. District membership comes from each school’s postcode (ONS postcode directory, via postcodes.io). Absence and exclusions for the district are summed over its schools, including any predecessor or successor URNs. This document is generated from templates/district_report.qmd by R/20_district_reports.R, from data built by R/17_area_analysis.R, R/18_district_effects.R and R/19_trust_effects.R. Its format is described in AREA_REPORTS.md.
